headline: Strong JOLTS and midterm jitters lift long yields 6bp; oil slips to a 4-week low, metals fade
summary: A draft US–Iran memorandum via Qatar outweighed a limited US strike on Qeshm Island, so WTI eased to $96.09 and Brent to a four-week low of $103.60, while RBOB firmed 1.2% on a diesel-led product bid. Strong JOLTS and factory data plus Election Day fiscal nerves steepened the Treasury curve, with the 10-year up about 6bp to near 4.96% and the 2-year about 4bp to 4.63%. Higher yields knocked gold back to near $3,930 and silver under $50, and Bunds and OATs rose about 2bp as the French budget vote slipped.
drivers: Strong data and Election Day steepen the curve

September JOLTS openings jumped to 7.52 million vs 7.13 million expected, and factory orders and durables also beat. The 10-year rose about 6bp to near 4.96% and the 30-year about 6bp to 5.33%, while the 2-year gained about 4bp; December hike odds sat near 75%.
Iran talks keep the oil premium leaking

Reports that Washington approved a Qatar-brokered draft MOU outweighed a limited US strike on Qeshm Island that briefly lifted Brent above $107. WTI settled -$0.37 at $96.09 and Brent -$1.17 at $103.60, the lowest closes since Oct 14 and Oct 7.
Higher yields cap the metals bounce

Gold dipped to about $3,893 before ending near $3,930, with Comex Nov settling -$29.00 at $3,927.90, as rising real yields and hike pricing outweighed cheaper oil. Silver fell harder, settling -2.2% at $49.59, and the gold/silver ratio widened to about 79.
Euro bonds follow Treasuries; French budget slips

Bund yields rose 1–2bp with the 10-year near 3.33%, and OATs rose about 2bp to near 4.95%, keeping the spread near 162bp. The Assembly postponed its vote on the 2027 budget's revenue part with about 750 amendments still pending, and deputies expect to reject it.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled down 37¢ (-0.4%) at $96.09, its lowest since Oct 14; Jan Brent -1.1% at $103.60, a four-week low.
oil.why: Crude extended Monday's 7% slump, though far more gently, as reports that the US approved a Qatar-brokered draft MOU, with Iran easing its nuclear stance in return for some frozen assets, kept the talks alive. A limited US strike on Qeshm Island lifted Brent briefly above $107, but officials called it defensive and Trump ruled out major strikes before the vote. Dubai spreads near flat point to looser prompt supply.
oil.outlook: Bias lower in a $92–100 range while talks advance, with $93–95 the key support; a signed framework could test $90. A collapse in talks or a post-midterm escalation in Hormuz would push WTI quickly back above $100.
oil.watch: Midterm results, API tonight, EIA stocks Nov 4 and Russia–Ukraine–US talks Nov 10–11.

gas.note: Dec RBOB rose 3.54¢ (+1.2%) to $2.9355 after Monday's 8% drop; AAA pump average near $4.15, down 12¢ in a week.
gas.why: Gasoline bounced even as crude slipped, as refined products caught a bid led by diesel, which jumped 2.5% after a Ukrainian drone strike set fire to Russia's Yaroslavl refinery and Russia hit Ukrainian energy sites. Short covering after Monday's 25.6¢ plunge added. US fundamentals stay soft: last week's 3.9 million barrel gasoline build and fading autumn demand keep the national average sliding toward $4.
gas.outlook: Range $2.80–3.05 with a mild downside bias as crude's war premium drains and demand fades. A Gulf or Russian refinery outage that tightens product supply would put $3.05 back in play.
gas.watch: EIA stocks Nov 4, refinery restarts and US–Iran headlines.

gold.note: Spot ended near $3,930, down about 0.4% after a dip to about $3,893; Comex Nov settled -$29.00 (-0.7%) at $3,927.90.
gold.why: Gold gave back part of Monday's 2% bounce as Treasury yields climbed 4–6bp on a strong 7.52 million JOLTS print and the market kept about 75% odds of a December Fed hike, raising the cost of holding bullion. Analysts noted gold is still being sold to cover losses elsewhere rather than bought as a haven. Dip buyers defended the area under $3,900, and the World Gold Council halved its 2026 investment demand forecast.
gold.outlook: Choppy in a $3,850–4,000 range, biased slightly lower while hike pricing holds. A close above $4,000 would signal a washout low; a hot payrolls Nov 6 that locks in a December hike could break $3,850.
gold.watch: Midterm results, the refunding and ISM services Nov 4 and payrolls Nov 6.

silver.note: Spot fell about 1.7% to near $49.80, back under $50 after a low near $48.60; Comex Nov settled -2.2% at $49.59.
silver.why: Silver fell harder than gold as higher yields and Fed hike pricing hit the more volatile metal, with brokers citing broad deleveraging and caution before the midterm results rather than weaker fundamentals. It swung more than 5% from low to high during the session. The gold/silver ratio widened to about 79 from 78, showing silver lagging.
silver.outlook: Range $47–52 with a fragile bias. Holding the Oct 30 settle low near $49.10 keeps the base intact; a break opens $47, while a close back above $52 would show the liquidation is done.
silver.watch: ISM services Nov 4, China trade data and payrolls Nov 6.

us2y.note: Up about 4bp to near 4.63% on strong JOLTS; December hike odds near 75%.
us2y.why: The front end rose as September JOLTS openings surged to 7.52 million against 7.13 million expected, with hiring steady, and factory orders and durable goods also beat. That reinforced the view that the labour market can absorb a December hike, with CME FedWatch near 75%. Oil holding near $96 rather than falling further removed Monday's offset.
us2y.outlook: Range 4.55–4.70%. A firm ADP and payrolls this week would push it toward 4.70%; a weak jobs report or a sharp equity selloff could pull it back to 4.55%.
us2y.watch: ADP and ISM services Nov 4, payrolls Nov 6.

us5y.note: Up about 5bp to near 4.76%, tracking the strong data and a modest bear steepening.
us5y.why: The belly rose about 5bp as the 7.52 million JOLTS print and beats in factory orders and durables pointed to resilient growth despite the AI-led stock wobble. With December hike odds near 75% and less easing priced for 2027, the 5-year took most of the data shock alongside the front end, while Election Day fiscal worries added a little term premium.
us5y.outlook: Range 4.65–4.85%. Strong ADP, ISM services and payrolls would test 4.85%; soft data or a risk-off move after the midterms could pull it back toward 4.65%.
us5y.watch: Refunding, ADP and ISM services Nov 4, payrolls Nov 6.

us10y.note: Up about 6bp to near 4.96%, the biggest rise in a week; 2s10s steepened to about 33bp.
us10y.why: The 10-year rose about 6bp as strong JOLTS, factory orders and durables data met Election Day nerves over fiscal policy, with strategists warning that a Democratic House would bring debt-ceiling and spending uncertainty and keep term premium high. Oil steadying near $96 removed Monday's support, and 10-year breakevens held near 2.31%, so most of the move came in real yields.
us10y.outlook: Range 4.85–5.05%. A close above 5% would open the October highs near 5.05%; a weak payrolls or a divided government that limits fiscal expansion could pull it back to 4.85%.
us10y.watch: Midterm results, the refunding Nov 4, payrolls Nov 6.

us30y.note: Up about 6bp to near 5.33%, matching the 10-year as the curve steepened.
us30y.why: The long bond rose about 6bp, mostly on term premium, as investors weighed the midterms' fiscal risks, including debt-ceiling mechanics next year, alongside strong JOLTS and factory data. Long yields are the most exposed to deficit worries and to oil-driven inflation risk, and with Brent still above $100 the long end gave back Monday's rally in full.
us30y.outlook: Range 5.25–5.40%. A larger refunding or an election result pointing to more borrowing would test 5.40%; a divided government and a steady Treasury plan could ease it toward 5.25%.
us30y.watch: Midterm results and the refunding Nov 4.

de2y.note: Up about 1bp to near 3.03%; markets still price a December ECB hike at well over 80%.
de2y.why: The Schatz barely moved because December ECB pricing was already high, at about 83–88% for a 25bp hike, after Kazimir warned on Monday that markets may still underestimate how much tightening is needed. Firmer Treasuries and a bounce in oil off Monday's lows nudged it up, while weak German data such as September's 2.0% retail sales drop limited selling.
de2y.outlook: Range 2.95–3.10%. A hot euro inflation print or hawkish ECB speakers would push toward 3.10%; a further oil slump easing energy inflation could pull it back to 2.95%.
de2y.watch: ECB speakers this week and the ECB on Dec 17.

de5y.note: Up about 2bp to near 3.13%, following Treasuries higher.
de5y.why: The 5-year rose about 2bp as the selloff in Treasuries after strong US JOLTS data spilled over to Europe, and UK gilts rose about 4bp ahead of Thursday's expected BoE hike. With the ECB priced to hike in December and oil steadying, the belly gave back part of Monday's oil-driven gains.
de5y.outlook: Range 3.05–3.20%. A sustained oil slide would pull it toward 3.05%; firm euro inflation or an oil rebound above $110 Brent would test 3.20%.
de5y.watch: BoE Nov 5 and US payrolls Nov 6.

de10y.note: Up about 2bp to near 3.33%, after Monday's nine-week low near 3.29%.
de10y.why: Bunds tracked Treasuries lower in price as US yields climbed about 6bp on strong data and midterm fiscal worries, and gilts sold off ahead of the BoE. Brent's smaller drop, to $103.60, gave less support than Monday's 7% slump, while energy-driven inflation keeps ECB hike bets near 85%.
de10y.outlook: Range 3.25–3.40%. A US–Iran deal that drives Brent below $100 would favour a retest of 3.25%; a hot US payrolls or oil rebound would push back toward 3.40%.
de10y.watch: BoE Nov 5, US payrolls Nov 6 and US–Iran headlines.

de30y.note: Up about 1bp to near 3.70%, lagging the front as the Bund curve stayed steady.
de30y.why: The long Bund rose only about 1bp as cheaper oil compared with last week and steady German supply limited the spillover from the 6bp jump in US long yields. Investors still demand a term premium for Germany's larger borrowing plans, but there was no new supply or fiscal news on the day.
de30y.outlook: Range 3.62–3.75%. A deeper oil slump would pull it toward 3.62%; heavy long-dated issuance or a US long-end selloff through 5.40% would push toward 3.75%.
de30y.watch: German auctions and US long yields after the refunding Nov 4.

fr2y.note: Up about 2bp to near 3.64%, in line with the euro front end.
fr2y.why: Short OATs rose with the euro front end as December ECB hike pricing held above 80% and Treasuries sold off on strong US data. The delay to the National Assembly's vote on the 2027 budget revenue part, with about 750 amendments still pending, added little at the front because the risk sits mostly in longer bonds.
fr2y.outlook: Range 3.55–3.70%, driven by ECB pricing more than politics. A hawkish ECB message would test 3.70%; softer energy and inflation would pull it toward 3.55%.
fr2y.watch: The budget revenue vote later this week and ECB speakers.

fr5y.note: Up about 2bp to near 4.31%, keeping pace with Bunds.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT rose about 2bp, in line with Germany, as global yields climbed on strong US data. French politics stayed in focus: the Assembly pushed back its vote on the revenue part of the 2027 budget, deputies expect to reject it, and the government may pass it by Article 49.3 or by decree, but that was largely priced after Fitch's negative outlook.
fr5y.outlook: Range 4.20–4.40%. A budget forced through without a government crisis would favour 4.20%; a no-confidence motion or new rating action would push toward 4.40%.
fr5y.watch: The budget revenue vote this week and the Nov 5 OAT auction.

fr10y.note: Up about 2bp to near 4.95%; the spread to Bunds held near 162bp.
fr10y.why: French 10-year yields rose with Bunds as Treasuries sold off on strong JOLTS data, while Belgian and Italian debt also lagged on fiscal and supply worries. The National Assembly postponed its vote on the 2027 budget's revenue part, with about 750 amendments pending and deputies expecting a no vote, but markets already assume Prime Minister Lecornu will use Article 49.3 or decrees, so the spread was stable.
fr10y.outlook: Spread range 155–172bp with the 10-year capped near 5%. A budget passed without a government crisis would narrow it toward 155bp; a no-confidence vote or failed 49.3 would send it back toward 172bp and above 5%.
fr10y.watch: The budget revenue vote this week, the Nov 5 auction and S&P Nov 27.

fr30y.note: Up about 2bp to near 5.47%, staying near its highs.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT rose about 2bp as the long end tracked a 6bp rise in US long yields and investors kept demanding a premium for France's fiscal path. Fitch's negative outlook, a deficit seen stuck near 5.5% next year and the stalled budget debate keep long OATs the weakest part of the curve, though there was no fresh shock on the day.
fr30y.outlook: Range 5.38–5.55%. Weak demand at the Nov 5 auction or a government crisis would test 5.55%; a budget passed with no political fallout could ease it toward 5.38%.
fr30y.watch: The Nov 5 auction and the budget revenue vote.

watch: Next: US midterm results overnight, the US refunding, ADP, ISM services and EIA stocks Nov 4, the BoE and OAT auction Nov 5, payrolls Nov 6, Russia–Ukraine–US talks Nov 10–11 and the ECB Dec 17.
sources: Dow Jones via Morningstar (US and euro bonds)
